title: TensorSpine Editor Presentation Bindings 1
description: What the language's schemas cannot say about the places they describe: that an `instance_definition` is drawn as a node, a `value_binding` as an edge, that `bytes` is shown in MiB, that `add` prints as `+`, that a `shape` gets the axis-row editor, and what a name written in a document refers to. It is the editor's own file, `packages/ui/src/presentation.json`, and the one data file the interface carries (the editor plan's §1); every key is a JSON pointer into a schema, resolved at startup.

anchor.description: `<$id>#<JSON pointer>`: the identity the registry indexes a schema under, `#`, and an RFC 6901 pointer into that schema's document. `…/model.json#` is the whole schema and `…/model.json#/$defs/instance_definition` one of its definitions. The same anchor the store computes for a place of a document (`Place.anchor`), so a binding and an occurrence are keyed by one scheme.

binding.description: What is bound to the place the key names. A binding says nothing the schema already says: a select's options are the schema's `enum`, a union's tags are the `required` keys of its members, and help text is the schema's `description`.

role.description: How the construct is drawn on the canvas: a node card, a composition box, a value edge, an interface terminal.

side.description: Which side of the canvas a terminal sits on: inputs enter on the left, outputs leave on the right.

face.description: The members shown on the node's face, in the order they are shown. Each one is a member the definition at this anchor declares; the audit checks it.

structuralSummary.description: Whether the face carries the summary of the instance's structural arguments. Which arguments those are is the core's answer (`describe`), never a list here.

label.description: What labels the construct. `$key` is the name of the map member it is written under — a value binding's rule name, which is how `--view` labels an edge.

widget.description: The editor bound to this construct where the generic walker has no reading of its own: the physical-name token editor, the expression and condition trees, the axis-row shape editor, the ordered rule list. A construct with no widget renders generically, which is the plan's own answer for one nobody has bound yet.

references.description: What a picker inside that editor offers, by the member each referent is named under: quantities and indices on the model side, argument paths on the unit side.

picker.description: The list a select at this place is filled from when it is not an enumeration: the axes and the precision roles the gathered library declares and the versions it carries of the primitive an instance pins, which the core answers; and the family names the workspace's own documents already write, which the editor reads off the documents it holds.

create.description: The label of the action offered beside that picker when what is wanted does not exist yet.

prefix.description: What is printed before a name written at this place, so that the text form of an expression tells one kind of name from another: an index prints `$layer` where a quantity prints `d`, and a parser reads the two apart (the editor plan's §4.13, artboard S7). Absent, a name prints bare.

symbols.description: A symbol per value of the enumeration at this anchor, or per tag of the union at it. An operator with no symbol prints and parses as `name(args)` and is listed by the startup audit as rendered generically, which is why `min` and `max` have none.

keywords.description: The word written before each member of the construct at this anchor, in a text form that writes them one after another: `if … then … else …` (the editor plan's §4.13). A symbol cannot say it — a symbol names one operator and stands in one place, before its operand, between two, or around a list — and a conditional expression has three operands, each introduced by a word of its own. The keys are members the definition declares and the order they are written in is the schema's, not the file's; the audit checks the first and the text form reads the second.

format.description: How a figure at this place is shown: a size in B/KiB/MiB/GiB with the exact number in the tooltip, a count of elements, a count of operations in `op`/`Mop`/`Gop`, a per-stream count, an epistemic status as a chip, a shape as its axes and extents. The renderings are `tools/view.py`'s own, which the editor takes over when that script is removed (the editor plan's finding F6). No component converts or rounds a figure of its own; the derived document's number is the fact and this is its rendering.

statusBar.description: This figure is one of the status bar's totals (the editor plan's §4.2 and §4.18: D3 total bytes, D5 operations per element, D4 append bytes per cached position, D2 peak live bytes per element). Which four they are is a choice the derived schema cannot state, so it is stated here and the bar shows what it finds rather than four places named in a component.

order.description: Where it sits in the bar, left to right, in the order §4.2 writes the fields.

label.description: What is written beside the figure, since the schema's member name is not a label a bar can carry. English, and the key of the interface's own dictionary (§4.21).

declares.description: The kind of thing the map at this anchor declares — a quantity, an instance, a composition, a site, an index, a public input. The name a command and the log use for it.

scope.description: The anchor of the declaration this one lives inside, when its references are read against it. A site and an index are declared inside a composition, so both name the anchor of the compositions map.

refers.description: Where a name declared here is referred to. The empty list is a statement: nothing in a document names a public output, so renaming one rewrites nothing.

form.description: Where it is printed: between its arguments, before its argument, or as a function name. Not inferable from the arity — `negate` and `absolute` are both unary and print `-a` and `abs(a)`, `add` and `min` both n-ary and print `a + b` and `min(a, b)`.

precedence.description: How tightly an infix symbol binds, so that a text form parenthesises exactly where it must and nowhere else: `layers - 1` needs no parentheses, `$layer mod 5 = 4` needs none either, and `(a + b) * c` needs one. Larger binds tighter. An operator's enumeration says nothing about how a reader groups it, so the numbers are here and a parser reads the same ones. Absent on an infix symbol, every nested application is parenthesised — always correct, rarely readable.

reference_rule.description: One way a name declared at this anchor is referred to, as the store's reference index reads occurrences. The schemas say which members hold a name; no keyword says what the name refers to, and this is where that is written down.

tag.description: The member the name is written under: the tag of a tagged value (`quantity`, `site`, `instance`), or the member the map is for a key (`indices`).

kind.description: `key` for a name written as a map's own member name, `tagged` for one written as the value of a member. Absent, both.

under.description: Restricts the rule to the occurrences at or below the enclosing declaration's place — how a composition's own scope is stated. The binding must name a `scope`.

scopedBy.description: The member that must carry the enclosing declaration's name beside the occurrence: `{"kind": "generated", "composition": "decoder", "instance": "attn_n"}` names a site of `decoder` from outside it. The binding must name a `scope`.

without.description: The members that must be *absent* beside the occurrence. A root instance is named by an `instance` written with no `composition` beside it, which is how a root selector is told from a generated one without naming either.
